question: How do record and matched object references calibrate the preserved nested statistic under known independent, unique and literal-copy laws?
outcome: Three thousand observed populations and 396,000 references audited. At nominal 5%, independent records reject 5.0%, uniqueness-conditioned records 5.9%, and literal copies reject 5.4% with object references versus 15.9% with record references. Paired excess 10.5 points, 500-cluster interval 8.5–12.6.
challenge: Copied reference streams have 500 linked trial pairs; copying also changes the physical-block premise required for fitting support bounds.
remedy: Preserve actual seeds, audit all 928,424 proposals and p-values, replay 33 complete fits and resample linked clusters for the paired interval. Audit constructive component bounds separately.
retry_when: A new observation or selection law changes the conditional space; do not rerun the same frozen calibration merely to improve its rates.

question: Which original conditional laws admit a component lower bound that guarantees nonempty nested folds?
outcome: One complete string per physical block yields one component per distinct string. Preserved slot inventories bound singleton references at eight and matched literal-copy references at six to eight. All 3,000 margins, 396,000 groupings and 29,169 allocation cases passed the audit. The bound's copy premise fails in all 99,000 record-copy references.
challenge: Nonidentical faces can join many complete strings through one physical component, invalidating a slot-inventory bound without its physical premise.
remedy: State the premise, prove the positive-weight allocator argument, regenerate 198,000 copy references and test 583,380 outer/inner splits without changing fitted scores.
retry_when: A new physical graph structure supplies a different support premise or needs an explicit total score.

question: Can an independently observed pooled inventory resolve numerical values when local account membership is unreliable?
outcome: Two hundred fresh base seeds generate 1,400 worlds and 11,200 prefixes. Under four swaps and 50% local support, complete-pool conservation changes correct/wrong/ambiguous outcomes from 133/9/58 to 190/1/9. Misdeclared completeness gives fifteen wrong accepted points. One wrong baseline passes eight rank-one fresh relations but fails independent counts.
challenge: The whole inventory must be independently available and complete; redundant fresh relations can preserve a wrong numerical ray. A static checker initially misclassified a local comprehension variable as hidden-key access.
remedy: Freeze observation availability, impose the collective relation without adding a support vote, retain inequalities and both scale views, independently verify all subset states and residuals, and preserve the checker repair beside unchanged inference hashes.
retry_when: New physical inventory observations, measured acquisition costs or independently ranked validation rows change the available constraints.
